# Quantum Erasure Budget Metrology

> Sharp local Fisher information and an attaining spin probe for parallel phase sensing after flagged loss.

## Story

- [README](README.md): task, main results, worked numerical case and reproduction.
- [Science route](science/README.md): how loss refinement, minimax estimation and coherent readout fit together.
- [Model](science/model.md): parallel phase, arbitrary fixed locations, local operating point and protected memory.

## Theorems

- [Optimal probe and readout](science/optimal-probe.md): finite-N local QFI ceiling, beta-binomial Dicke probe, modular syndrome and saturating measurement.
- [Random count](science/loss-distributions.md): simultaneous optimality at fixed input variance and scalar optimization for a count law.
- [Protected memory](science/memory.md): necessary dimension for exact saturation and unassisted constructions.

## Study and reproduce

- [Watrous bridge](learning/WATROUS_BRIDGE.md): from states, channels and measurements to the physical receiver.
- [Milestones](learning/MILESTONES.md): 30 questions through the theory and protocol.
- [Worked example](learning/WORKED_EXAMPLE.md): four sensors, one erasure, no protected register.
- [Attribution](references/RELATED_WORK.md): what the antecedents already prove.
- [Finite checks](verification/README.md): commands and check coverage.

The FI is local to a chosen nominal phase. The protected register is counted by its Hilbert-space dimension. In the converse, granting erased bits only enlarges the available information; the physical readout uses its encoded syndrome and the survivors.
